_note: 72 original JAMB-style Section A questions on The Lekki Headmaster (authored 2026-11-12, independently verified against the OCR'd scan — 16 wording slips fixed then), PLUS 35 extension items authored 2026-11-13 from content-folder/lekki-headmaster-summary.md, deduped against the originals (near-duplicates dropped at author time; an invented proverb removed, not fixed). Total 107 items: coverage spans all 12 chapters and the under-represented skills (setting, technique, vocabulary, character, sub-plot, inference). Every item: topic=comprehension-and-summary, options a–d, answer in options, explanation attached. For internal paper-construction reference; not shown to learners as-is. Do not seed to production without explicit go/no-go.

questions.question: How did Stardom Schools' lateness problem transform after the boarding fees were cut from N250,000 to N165,000?

options.text: More than 80 per cent of parents moved their children into boarding, and almost all pupils reached assembly by 7:45am
Parents protested the fee increase and kept their children at home
The school suspended morning assemblies altogether
Lateness got worse because the fee was lowered

questions.explanation: The boarding incentive moved most families into the hostels, so assembly attendance improved sharply.

questions.question: What does Ikenna Egbu's account of the Jos excursion reveal about his character?

options.text: He favours the UK over every Nigerian city
He is proud of Nigeria and would rather settle in Jos than japa abroad
He has never seen waterfalls or dams before
He secretly prefers drama over science subjects

questions.explanation: Ikenna closes his Jos narration by declaring he would rather settle there than migrate to Canada or London.

questions.question: What is the most likely reason Bepo breaks down at the podium during assembly?

options.text: The WASSCE results had just been announced
Ikenna's Jos speech reminds him of Nigeria's beauty while Seri and his children are already in London
He was fired unexpectedly by the MD that morning
The school anthem had not been rehearsed

questions.explanation: His breakdown follows a patriotic Jos narrative — a sharp contrast to his own emigration plan. The cause is only confirmed later, in Chapter 2.

questions.question: What is the rule on F9 scores at Stardom Schools?

options.text: The teacher in that subject is considered for instant dismissal
The student is suspended for a term
Parents are fined
The teacher is only reprimanded verbally

questions.explanation: Even the MD's cousin Funso Daniels was not spared an abrupt exit — the text implies F9s, not Ds, were fatal; the two D-scoring teachers were rewarded, not sacked.

questions.question: What did Stardom substitute for normal prayers on Tuesdays and Thursdays?

options.text: Endless announcements from the principal
The second stanza of Nigeria's National Anthem
No prayer at all
Eid prayer for the whole school

questions.explanation: Tuesday and Thursday assemblies opened with the second stanza of the Anthem, taken as their prayer.

questions.question: Why is Bepo called 'The Lekki Headmaster'?

options.text: He owns land around Lekki
He imitated the old Village Headmaster from an old TV drama, and insisted the word 'principal' is pronounced 'PrinciPL'
He studied in Lekki
He founded Stardom Schools

questions.explanation: Both habits are recalled in the text: mimicry of the Village Headmaster on TV, and his 'PrinciPL' pronunciation correction.

questions.question: What decision does Bepo finally admit after five days of interrogation?

options.text: He will resign next week
He will leave Nigeria for the United Kingdom to join Seri and the children
He will start a school of his own in Lagos
He will retire at 50

questions.explanation: Chapter 2 is titled 'The Enticement' — Bepo finally names his plan to join Seri in the UK.

questions.question: Which consideration still makes Bepo hesitant to accept the UK teaching role?

options.text: The post comes with a lower salary
His love for Stardom's learners and his refusal to abandon a developing nation for an already-developed one
Seri wants to return to Nigeria
He failed the visa interview

questions.explanation: He feels guilty leaving learners behind in a developing nation to serve a developed one — the salary debate is only the surface quarrel.

questions.question: What argument does Audu use to persuade Bepo over his wife's salary objection?

options.text: If Bepo sends £1,000 home monthly, that alone beats his ₦400,000 Stardom pay
Seri will lose her nursing licence in the UK
The UK is too expensive for teachers
Bepo cannot teach English in London

questions.explanation: Audu fantasises about emigrating himself and converts £1,000 remittance to roughly ₦1.7 million — dwarfing the principal's salary.

questions.question: At roughly what age does Bepo plan to retire from Stardom?
questions.explanation: Retirement at 55 is four years away at this point in the book; he was also exploring business ventures for retirement.

questions.question: What was the fate of Bepo's small neighbourhood school, Fruitful Future?

options.text: It was taken over by Stardom
It grew into three campuses
It crumbled after post-service challenges — roads failed, a pipe burst and residents fled
It was relocated to Abuja

questions.explanation: The failed school becomes relevant in Chapter 7, where its collapse recurs when Bepo recalls his first foray into entrepreneurship.

questions.question: Which subjects did Bepo study at University of Benin?

options.text: Physics and Mathematics Education
Chemistry and Biology Education
English and History Education
Business Administration

questions.explanation: The text recalls Bepo practised as an English teacher after training in English/History at University of Benin.

questions.question: According to Bepo's friend in the USA, what were typical daily earnings and monthly cap?

options.text: $50–100 per day, max $800 a month
$150–250 per day, up to four days a week, ≈ $2,400 a month
$500–1,000 per day, $20,000 a month
$80 per day, $1,600 a month

questions.explanation: The migrant friend quotes $150–$250 daily, roughly $2,400 monthly at four days a week.

questions.question: What does the Yoruba proverb 'oga ta, oga o ta, owo alaaru a pe' imply?

options.text: An employee never works a full day
The employer must always lose money first
However the employer performs, the employee still takes full pay
Yoruba workers are the hardest workers in the world

questions.explanation: The proverb notes that the worker earns regardless — a pillar of Bepo's admiration for wage honesty in developed systems.

questions.question: Where does Sola and her husband live, and how did they survive the move?

options.text: London; they sent for extended family first
Manchester, in a non-furnished two-bedroom at £650 per month; her husband pursues a Master's while she works
Birmingham; she works as a nurse full-time
Edinburgh; they stayed with relatives

questions.explanation: Sola describes the Manchester flat and the £650 non-furnished arrangement, with her husband studying while she works.

questions.question: Which example best illustrates that age grants no exemption from manual labour abroad?

options.text: Akindele, aged 55, enduring 12-hour shifts in the corrections service
Hope's wife leaving him mid-course
Riike buying houses in Ibadan
Sola's child Betty escaped asthma in London

questions.explanation: Akindele — invited by a US citizen after working in a Lagos media house — does freight loading then corrections, warning that even retired permanent secretaries pick up casual jobs in the US.

questions.question: What is the central lesson Hope's story teaches about migrant marriage?

options.text: Marriage is a contract and can be signed again abroad
Spouses who fund a partner's study may stop paying without warning, and the earner's own parents may side with the earner
Nigerians abroad love studying
Accountants migrate faster than nurses

questions.explanation: Hope's wife stops sponsoring him after four months; his complaints to her Nigerian parents end fruitless — a caution about funding one side of a partnership abroad.

questions.question: Which migration-related scandal shook Stardom before Bepo left?

options.text: The WASSCE results were forged
Mr Nku took a N2 million school-cooperative loan and vanished into the Japa wind
The MD was arrested for embezzling the cooperative
A driver stole exam scripts

questions.explanation: Nku's disappearance with the school-cooperative loan, and a driver who tried to steal a school bus for his son abroad, are the two named scandals.

questions.question: What is the reason the embassy denied Mr Ibe's family's London visa?

options.text: Bank proof of funds was incomplete
A DNA test showed one child was not Ibe's biological child
Mr Ibe was arrested at the appointment
Mrs Ignatius failed her English test

questions.explanation: The DNA-based paternity result for Favour (SS2) unravelled the emigration plan and split the family.

questions.question: What does Mrs Ignatius's late-night call to Bepo reveal about the parent–principal relationship at Stardom?

options.text: All parents keep the relationship strictly official
Some parents overstretch the cordiality and treat school staff as counsellors
Teachers always defend erring parents
School wireless lines are impossible to reach

questions.explanation: Mrs Ignatius discussed her marital affairs with Bepo at 11:55pm — Bepo observes some parents overstretch his tolerance by treating him as a confidant.

questions.question: Bibi was eventually reassigned to Green House. Why?

options.text: The fees for other houses were lower
The gripes — Mr Wala-Ayesoro with deep facial marks frightened the child in her sleep and on the basketball court
The school ordered the transfer
Ayesoro was promoted

questions.explanation: After Ayesoro's attempts to calm her fear of his tribal marks failed, Bibi had to be reassigned to Green House, where Tim belonged; the school's drastic step for the fallout was transferring Ayesoro to Stardom Hub.

questions.question: What drastic step did the Stardom management take over Mr Ayesoro?

options.text: He was sacked instantly
He was transferred to the property wing — Stardom Hub
He was demoted to clerk
He was given a one-year suspension

questions.explanation: To avoid losing Bibi and her siblings to a rival school, the school moved Ayesoro from teaching into property management.

questions.question: What do the Ignatius, Ladele/Ayesoro and visa episodes share?

options.text: All three mock the government
All expose how family life and safety can collapse when pressures on migration or fear overwhelm calm judgement
All concern officials at Stardom
All led to resignations

questions.explanation: Lower-stakes classroom fear and high-stakes paternity/visa destruction are mirrored — private fragility drives public outcomes.

questions.question: Why does Bepo reflect on writing a memoir as he lies awake thinking?

options.text: He is bored on holiday
The Ignatius case feels like the last straw — Stardom has given him endless material for a book like this
The MD asked him to
Seri asked him to distract himself

questions.explanation: He considers chronicling Stardom's defining incidents in a professional biography once he reaches the UK — material the case itself supplies.

questions.question: What does Mrs Ibidun Gloss discover when she inspects the back-gate land?

options.text: A secret building site
About half of the three plots filled with teachers' cars and two buses
A warehouse of co-operative property
The remains of a car accident

questions.explanation: The MD walks the school land and finds teachers' personal vehicles parked there instead of the official car park.

questions.question: What was the official answer to how teachers afforded those cars?

options.text: They stole the school's purse
Stardom Cooperative Society — mostly fellow staff took loans, deducted from source, in excess of N50 million of N95 million saved
Banks offered them automatic loans
The principals paid them from discretionary funds

questions.explanation: The MD learns about the cooperative's N95 million purse, more than half loaned out to staff.

questions.question: What new borrowing rules did the family board impose on the cooperative after the inspection?

options.text: A complete lending freeze with the MD holding the only key
Borrowing capped at N250,000 per staff member, MD approval required for each loan, and management informed of the cooperative's elections
Car purchases banned outright for all staff
Only senior staff may borrow

questions.explanation: The board feared staff might split off and found their own school with the cooperative's money; it capped loans and required MD sign-off.

questions.question: What does 'hanging a snake in the roof' imply, as the MD's mother Chief Mrs Bayo puts it?

options.text: Staff are incapable of rebellion
A quiet, loaded danger everyone ignores; the cooperative could become the education rival that ousts Stardom
The MD feared snakes in her office
Cooperative elections are always rigged

questions.explanation: Metaphor: an unmanaged risk lurking above heads — the staff could appropriate the brand, funds and ideas to found a rival school.

questions.question: What is the MD's privately-hidden health condition?

options.text: Hypertension
Chronic spine surgery recovery
Chronic sitting-related buttock pain after 30-plus years, managed with brief rests in her private office
A rare skin condition

questions.explanation: The MD's private room exists so she can rest; almost no one at Stardom knows why.

questions.question: Which theme does the cooperative controversy illuminate most directly?

options.text: Academic excellence at all costs
Perverse wealth — staff finances can arm a future rival, so the managers clamp down on leaks in the purse
Romance in the workplace
Cooperatives are illegal in Nigeria

questions.explanation: Chapter 5 reveals the double-edged purse: staff perks can empower a competitor founded with Stardom's own ideas and savings.

questions.question: What is the alleged error in the notebooks that triggers the attempted dismissal of Mr Fafore?

options.text: 'Ade as well as Jide come early'
'Ade as well as Jide comes early' — the MD demands a plural verb after 'as well as'
'Ade as well as Jide are early'
'Ade as well as Jide be early'

questions.explanation: The MD and Mr Guta attacked the singular 'comes'; Bepo insists standard grammar requires it after 'as well as'.

questions.question: Which English rule does Bepo invoke to defend Fafore?

options.text: Use singular verb after 'as well as', 'together with', 'alongside' etc.
Use plural verbs with collective nouns
Use subjunctive forms for contrary-to-fact conditions
English always agrees with the second noun

questions.explanation: Conjunction phrases like 'as well as' take the singular verb in standard English — confirmed by every staff member checking online.

questions.question: What does Fafore's work schedule reveal about him?

options.text: He arrives late routinely
He is lazy
He is extremely industrious — he wakes by 4:00am, leaves home at 4:30am, and reaches Stardom by 6:00am
He only teaches computer studies

questions.explanation: Fafore commutes from Ogun State via a self-built unplastered house, making the early commute his life — hence his punctuality awards.

questions.question: Which previous lawsuit makes Stardom staff hesitant to pair students with note-copying?

options.text: The refund of 50% of tuition award case
A parent sued after a girl with neat handwriting copied notes on the board; the school settled out of court, paid one tuition-free term, and the teacher sat out three months without pay
The bank collapsed
The proprietor was fined for corruption

questions.explanation: Stardom stopped note-copying (not lesson relaying) after the lawsuit over a girl dogged into a teacher's service.

questions.question: What personal history fuels Bepo's sympathy for Fafore?

options.text: Bepo grew up as a wealthy man
Bepo once 'ate' a tenant's N2,500 electricity tariff while jobless — and suffered public humiliation as 'Oga Tisa' when truth surfaced
Bepo is a qualified barrister
Bepo was suspended once

questions.explanation: He recalls 'Oga Tisa' and the Iya Mathew elubo dunking — first-hand shame of poverty he never wants a colleague to taste.

questions.question: How does Mr Audu restore harmony after the faulty sack attempt?

options.text: He organises a protest
He stages a mock trial — grants the MD 'pardon' and bows theatrically, breaking the tension with laughter
He weeps with the MD
He resigns in solidarity

questions.explanation: Audu pronounces Fafore correct and acquits the MD — 'And the MD, Mrs. Ibidun Gloss, is hereby pardoned, discharged and acquitted' — and the room rocks with laughter.

questions.question: What correction did Bepo want made at Beesway Group of School?

options.text: Add 'International' to the name
Change 'Group of School' to 'Group of Schools' — a group implies more than one school
Drop the word 'Group' completely
Rename it after the founding father

questions.explanation: Bepo kept insisting the collective noun 'group' required a plural — Meko fended him off with divine-inspiration and spiritual-undertone rhetoric, not a blasphemy charge.

questions.question: What does Bepo discover at 2:30am during the ritual?

options.text: The school canteen catching fire
Men burying a large white cow alive in a pit on the school premises, under the director's supervision
Teachers' cars being burned
Students stealing exam scripts

questions.explanation: Floodlights go off; Bepo sees shapes — five men, a cord/halter — around a cow being steered into a pit; he challenges them and is beaten; the director urges 'handle him gently'.

questions.question: What did Mr Ogo want to sell Bepo for his school's future?

options.text: A Bible story curriculum for N35,000
A ritual — flinging corn grains to supernaturally flood the school with pupils for N35,000
A year of free advertising
Parent cooperation lists

questions.explanation: Ogo offered occult inflation of enrolment; Bepo refused, built enrolment properly to over 70, but the school failed from road collapse and pipe burst without any relocation reward.

questions.question: Who does Bepo see arrested on TV ten years later?

options.text: Egi Meko, accused of misappropriation
Mr Ogo — the very man who once offered him an enrolment ritual now accused of murdering a client he had fleeced of N29m
His wife Seri
His former colleague from Fruitful Future

questions.explanation: Watching the news, Bepo sees an old parent carried off in handcuffs for the 'spiritual' pit death of a woman paying for fertility treatment.

questions.question: Why does Bepo finally decide not to report the Beesway ritual?

options.text: He fears the legal and financial cost and possible reprisals
He was given N500,000 to keep quiet
Seri begged him to drop it
He had been promoted

questions.explanation: He weighs legal bills, fossilised police, and likely retaliation; decides the cost outweighs the benefit; the director's 'special prayer for my late father' explanation is the trigger, not the excuse.

questions.question: What is the novel's position on shortcuts via ritual, as expressed in this chapter?

options.text: Ritual is useful when fee pressures demand it
Shortcuts betray the trust institutions carry — honesty in method matters even when results are slow or fail
Directors should run every meeting with a cow
Only wealthy schools need ritual

questions.explanation: The case for patient honest education: Bepo's small school grew from real quality, even though it later failed honestly; the ritual shortcut offered and the director's prayer both expose the trap.

questions.question: How much did Head Boy and Head Girl nomination forms cost?
questions.explanation: Head Boy/Girl forms were N50,000; their deputies N40,000; all other offices N25,000.

questions.question: What does the MD's debtor rule — 'If you want a debtor to lead fee payers, ask a tenant to lead the landlord' — mean?

options.text: Tough behaviour from tenants is expected
One who owes the school should not lead those who pay — leadership must come from a good debt-free antecedent
Landlords make great leaders
Only landlords may contest prefect positions

questions.explanation: It is the strongest debt-free requirement in the selection process.

questions.question: Why did Tosh storm out of the Speech Day hall?

options.text: He lost his own form
Banky, in his speech, called him 'the son of an ex-convict'
The microphone failed
His father arrived unexpectedly

questions.explanation: Tosh's father had been detained 36 months on misappropriation charges; he'd been released, but the label 'ex-convict' stung enough to walk out.

questions.question: What is Tosh's father's official status today?

options.text: Convicted of all counts
He spent 36 months in detention, faced trial over a N2.5 billion contract sum, was released, and his company was ordered to refund the sum — the court did not find him directly guilty
He is in hiding
He was cleared before detention

questions.explanation: The novel flags the same incident that fuels the Banky–Tosh feud — parents can be political rivals on the PDP/APC axis — and their families dispute even this legacy now.

questions.question: What is the 'Breath Project' that Bepo is in danger of losing?

options.text: A plant garden for oxygen
A five-year invention-club effort to manufacture a phone from recycled parts, co-funded by the school and the Life Grid NGO
A breathing exercise for prefects
A school sports team

questions.explanation: He swears to fly back from London for the launch — the phone is Stardom's public stamp of scientific achievement.

questions.question: Why do the parents — not the students — drive the Banky–Tosh dispute?

options.text: The students lack personality
Two warring politician fathers (Progressives All Congress and Democratic People's Party) project old rivalries — a dance contest 3–2 loss, a PTA treasurer's position — onto their sons' public names
They are alumni donors
Tosh is adopted by the Ogbas

questions.explanation: Bepo close to both camps sees that the boys inherit conflict they did not start — the dispute is an adult political axis mapped onto adolescents.

questions.question: What does Stardom do each term, according to the philosophy Bepo sold to the management?

options.text: Holds a weekly assembly abroad
Runs one excursion per term to an attraction within the country plus one annual international excursion
Organises no travel at all
Flies every student to London every year

questions.explanation: Bepo insisted students know their own country before they meet the world — decades of trips to waterfalls, reserves, cities and coasts.

questions.question: Which waterfall does the text rank highest in West Africa?

options.text: Erin-Ijesa (Olumirin) Waterfalls, Osun State
Ikogosi Warm Springs, Ekiti State
Owu Waterfalls, Kwara State — 120 metres high, 330 feet of escarpment
Gurara Falls, Niger State

questions.explanation: Owu in Kwara is described as the highest in West Africa at 120m above water level and 330 feet down.

questions.question: How does The Lekki Headmaster account for the discovery of the Ikogosi Warm Springs?

options.text: Discovered in 1140 AD by Akinla, first of the town of Erin-Ijesa
Discovered in 1852 by Rev. John S. McGee, from a mission base at Igede-Ekiti — after defying native warnings
Built by Shell in 1925
Known to Yoruba hunters since 1200

questions.explanation: McGee defied warnings and wrote about it for Royal Ambassador work, leading eventually to government takeover as a youth camp.

questions.question: What does the Yoruba proverb 'Ile la tii ke'eko rode' teach?

options.text: Everyone's home ultimately belongs alone
Charity begins at home
Trade is king
Kings must travel

questions.explanation: Bepo cites it at the Lagos-tourism passage — home ground must be known and loved before learners meet the world.

questions.question: How does the Badagry visit change Bepo?

options.text: He becomes a historian
He begins to see voluntary emigration into 'japa' as a modern replica of the forced trans-Atlantic slave trade — Africans rushing onto their former masters' yards of their own will
He converts the students to Islam
He decides never to marry again

questions.explanation: At the Black Heritage Museum, Bepo connects slavery history and modern emigration — the pivot of the entire book.

questions.question: Why does Bepo rank sightseeing so highly for elite students?

options.text: To market the school to overseas universities
He was aware most students would be sent abroad after secondary education — and touching the country should anchor their love for it later
To distract them from examinations
To raise money for the Breath Project

questions.explanation: He believes deep country knowledge seeds lifelong attachment — many would simply never return.

questions.question: Why does Bepo go to Ibadan rather than Lagos to renew his passport?

options.text: Ibadan flights are cheaper
News of empty booklets and chaotic crowds in Lagos frightens him, and neighbouring states have less traffic
He lives there
Seri lives there

questions.explanation: He weighs his own options — Ikoyi and Ikeja swarmed with applicants and booklets ran out; smaller states would have fewer crowds. Tai the agent details come later.

questions.question: Who is Tai that handles Bepo's passport renewal?

options.text: A SENIOR immigration officer
An ordinary business-centre operator colluding with immigration staff — he charged ₦100,000 for the 10-year (64-page) passport; Bepo separately tipped the officer ₦2,000
A bank manager
A teacher colleague

questions.explanation: The law bans middlemen — yet reality assembles them anyway; Tai is a fixer, not a civil servant.

questions.question: What extra requirement keeps Bepo rooted in Ibadan for even longer?

options.text: An additional four-week wait for a new photograph
A NIN validation visit to the NIN office — and network glitches hold the validation up for another three weeks
Holding him for the other matter of the Japa court case
Obligatory police clearance

questions.explanation: The NIN validation visit caps the approval; his departure date threatens to slip as network problems stall the process.

questions.question: Which poem by J. P. Clark does Bepo recall on the Molete Bridge, and what does it describe?

options.text: A Nigerian note on the Limpopo
'Ibadan' — 'Ibadan, running splash of rust and gold', scattered among seven hills
'Logos' — on the lagoon
Ode to Liberian kings

questions.explanation: Bepo recognises the city's image from the poem and googles it to get the text right.

questions.question: What is the novel's attitude to the 'official online route' for passport acquisition?

options.text: It works smoothly for everyone
Neither endorsed nor celebrated — Bepo and others chose to avoid it because it's slow and erratic, and many suspect the delays are deliberate
It's faster than the office
The government fines those who try it

questions.explanation: Many abandon the online route for the office because it is slow and erratic; some suspect the glitches were deliberate to push people back to the office.

questions.question: Which theme does Chapter 10 dramatise through the passport queue?

options.text: Nigerians do not need travel documents
Formal bureaucratic pain — ordinary life is besieged by fraudulent workarounds and delays, so people pay touts to leap the queue
Nigeria is leaderless
Education solves all problems

questions.explanation: Passport pains dramatise institutional failure — real-world bedrock motivation for japa.

questions.question: What fee did Stardom pay to change Bepo's Emirates flight from Saturday to the following Saturday?

options.text: Free

questions.explanation: He called Emirates to shift the date by a week; a $100 fine was paid gladly by the school.

questions.question: Why does Bepo cry out 'Noooo!' during the canoe dance?

options.text: A prop falls
The canoe dance (learned from the National Troupe after an October show) transports him mentally back to the slave museum and the terror of the slave ships
He is mocked by dancers
His phone rings mid-show

questions.explanation: He vividly pictures the slaves and the whips; stunned audience silences; he snaps back and praises the performance.

questions.question: How did Chief David Aje originally hire Bepo?

options.text: A spontaneous handshake at an interview
He saw Bepo had poor references and rejected him
After one CV read and a single chat — no panel — Dad was 'stuck' on him; he was to resume on 14 September, resumed eight days late, and Aje stuck with him — the gamble paid off
He traded a car for Bepo's services

questions.explanation: Aje gambled on Bepo's CV and letters; appearing eight days late could have lost him the job; the gamble paid off 24 years later.

questions.question: What gift does the MD give Bepo, and what is it 'not less than'?

options.text: A house in Lekki
A domiciliary cheque — not less than $10,000, the highest Stardom has ever given a disengaging member of staff (after an absurd 'ten billion!' guess inflates the room)
A car
Three months of vacation

questions.explanation: The envelope is 'flat' — it's a cheque, not raw dollars; MD tees up the joke then tells the truth.

questions.question: What mock-speech habits did the farewell skit imitate?

options.text: His high-pitched singing
His trademark 'other way...' stall, the 'if you say education is too expensive — try' catchphrase, the 'PrinciPL' pronunciation, and hot temper with class
His British accent
His football skills

questions.explanation: The skit captures his signature — the 'other way...' stall, the popular saying completed in unison by students, the 'PrinciPL' correction culture, and his hot temper with an idle teacher.

questions.question: What does the farewell reveal about Stardom's culture of gratitude to long-serving educators?

options.text: They ignore long service altogether
Years of service are lavishly honoured; the school claims him publicly as its own heritage even while wishing him well elsewhere
Only sportsmen get celebrated
Gratitude is limited to cash totals

questions.explanation: Banner, MD's testimony, gift — the school makes plain that Bepo's loss will be felt deeply and is loudly mourned.

questions.question: Why is Bepo determined to arrive early at the airport this time?

options.text: Seri is already at the airport
He once misread an 11:00am ticket as 1:00pm; he missed the flight and flew the next day only after paying a $100 penalty
His plane is delayed
The VP wants to see him off

questions.explanation: The British Airways episode taught him to triple-check tickets — he leaves home at 3:00pm for a 10:00pm departure.

questions.question: What did Seri ask Bepo to buy from Oyingbo market as he packed?

options.text: Deep freeze and electronics
Iru (locust beans), egusi, ground crayfish, and dry snail — Nigerian ingredient export for her London cooking
Owo; goat; yam
A mobile phone

questions.explanation: Seri itemises iru (locust beans), egusi, ground crayfish and dry snail — Nigerian produce for her London kitchen.

questions.question: What happens in Bepo's dream at the airport, and how does he react when he wakes?

options.text: He dreams of teaching again and screams with joy
He is at the Heritage Slave Museum (counting seven million slaves); a white man shouts 'Enter!' and Bepo leaps from the seat and shouts 'Noooo!' before being calmed by officials
He dreams of his mother
He is chased by the police

questions.explanation: The dream is the novel's climax: slavery → voluntary migration → he almost embarks → he refuses (not via flight) and returns instead of leaving.

questions.question: What difference do Monday's students notice immediately?

options.text: New uniforms
No principal at the gate, no assembly dominance — the VP cannot replicate his authority
Shorter classes
The school visited abroad

questions.explanation: Without him, the morning feels flat — students demonstrate how much authority and presence he carried.

questions.question: Which theme is resolved by Bepo's spontaneous return?

options.text: That families should always reunite
That duty to country and community outweighs material migration incentives; his heart's true address is Stardom
That money never matters
That leadership does not matter

questions.explanation: He did not leave Stardom at all — 'My heart is here... to complete my mission!' is the book's closing thesis; the anthem confirms victory.

questions.question: How does the novel close?

options.text: On an uncertain note — we never learn whether Bepo missed his flight
Circular: dusk → dawn — students carry him on their shoulders as the school anthem declares 'We're Stars... yet Stardom Schools will win'
With a wedding between Bepo and Seri
With Seri flying home to Lagos permanently

questions.explanation: Bookending the 'dusk' of the opening breakdown, the book ends with dawn — his return, the anthem, and communal triumph.

questions.question: How long before the opening assembly had Stardom's pep-talk tradition been running?

options.text: About seven years
One term
About three years
Since Stardom was founded

questions.explanation: The assembly that opens the novel is thrown off-course at the very moment the pep talk — launched seven years earlier — has everyone excited.

questions.question: After the boarding fees were cut from ₦250,000 to ₦165,000, what did Stardom quietly raise to recover income?

options.text: Excursion and Other Items, by ₦93,000
The lunch levy, by ₦10,000
The uniform price, by ₦25,000
Nothing — the school had no way to recover the shortfall

questions.explanation: Above 80% of parents moved their children into boarding; the school then quietly raised Excursion and Other Items by ₦93,000 — the boarding-fee relief was not free.

questions.question: After Stardom's over-90% WASSCE pass rate, how much did teachers of distinction-scoring subjects receive?

options.text: ₦30,000, on top of the ₦20,000 all SSS 3 teachers received
₦50,000 each, flat
Nothing — the only celebration was snacks and wine
₦93,000 each, the same levy increase

questions.explanation: Every SSS 3 teacher received ₦20,000 in cash plus snacks and wine; teachers of distinction-scoring subjects received ₦30,000. Only Obong Ukaku (Chemistry) and Taye Kareem (Geography) had two-candidate D-lines to answer — and no one scored F9.

questions.question: Vice-Principal Grace Apeh ordered which teacher to close the assembly and send learners to classes?

options.text: Mr Justus Anabel, the chemistry teacher
Mr Oyelana, the CRK teacher
Mr Oye Wande, the physics teacher
Mr Audu, the fine arts teacher

questions.explanation: As Bepo lay broken on the podium, Apeh ordered Justus Anabel — chemistry — to dissolve the assembly and send learners to classes fast.

questions.question: How does the novel choose to open Chapter 1?

options.text: In the middle of the action — Bepo freezes at the podium mid-assembly and collapses into tears, with no preamble about his career
With a prologue tracing Bepo's childhood in Benin City before his first posting
With Seri phoning Bepo from London about the passport renewal
With the narrator explaining the founding of Stardom Schools

questions.explanation: The novel drops the reader straight into the morning of Bepo's breakdown — no history lesson, just a pep talk, an unexpected silence, and a man failing publicly. The reader learns who Bepo is only through the fragments people say and do around the collapse.

questions.question: Which pronunciation habit does Bepo insist on with his staff?

options.text: He insists it is 'PrinciPL', not 'Principo', and corrects anyone who says otherwise
He insists staff call him 'Chief Executive' at all times
He accepts 'Principo' with good-humoured grace and never corrects it
He bans the use of any title and demands plain 'Ade'

questions.explanation: The staffroom joke about him runs on two rails: King Oloja of 'Village Headmaster' (the nickname that stuck) and his own relentless 'it is PrinciPL, not Principo.'

questions.question: At the height of his financial drought, where did Bepo 'eat' ₦2,500 of tenants' electricity tariff money?

options.text: Tyana Ipaja — a crowded face-me-I-face-you house in Iyana Ipaja, Lagos
His self-built, unplastered house in Ifo, Ogun State
The Stardom staff quarters in Lekki
His father's compound in Benin City

questions.explanation: At Tyana Ipaja he collected the tariff on behalf of the other tenants and spent it; when NEPA disconnected the cable the furious tenants mocked him as 'Oga Tisa' and Iya Mathew dumped a bowl of elubo over his head. It is the cruelest shame he carries.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of Seri, Bepo's wife?

options.text: She works as a nurse in London and is the strongest force pressing Bepo to emigrate
She is a doctor in Kaduna who manages his health
She teaches at Stardom alongside him and is resigning on her own
She is a university lecturer in Ibadan who chairs Stardom's board

questions.explanation: Seri is the nurse in London who has long settled there with the children — Nike at university, Kike in secondary — and regularly presses Bepo on the phone about the passport and the move.

questions.question: What does the nickname 'Oga Tisa', which the Ipaja tenants gave Bepo, literally mean?

options.text: 'Teacher Oga' — a mocking label for a teacher reduced to joblessness and debt
'Lord of the market' — a trader's honorific
'Chief Accountant' — a payroll title
'Master Principal' — a term of respect used at Stardom

questions.explanation: 'Oga Tisa' fuses Yoruba/Pidgin address terms with the Portuguese 'Tisa' (teacher). The tenants sang 'Oga Tisa, ole! O na owo ina!' — 'Mr Teacher, thief! He spent the electricity tariff!'

questions.question: What is Mr Oyelana's counter-argument to Bepo's remittance arithmetic?

options.text: He will be spending in pounds, not naira — so comparing pound-pay to his naira salary does not work
He will be taxed so heavily that remittance is impossible
The pound is certain to crash within a year of his arrival
His teaching certificate will not be recognised in the UK

questions.explanation: Oyelana points out that pounds spent in London are not naira remitted home; Audu waves this off — 'if he sends £1,000 home a month, that is above ₦1.7 million — nobody making ₦400,000 can match that.'

questions.question: At about ₦1,700 per pound, what does Bepo's prospective UK monthly entitlement of about £3,600 come to?

options.text: About ₦6 million a month
About ₦600,000 a month
About ₦60 million a month
About ₦1.7 million a month

questions.explanation: £3,600 × ₦1,700 ≈ ₦6.1 million — versus his ₦400,000 Stardom salary. The arithmetic, not a sermon, is what keeps the offer alive in his mind.

questions.question: How many doctors, by the Nigerian government's own admission, emigrate every year?

options.text: About 3,000
About 300
About 9,000
None — emigration of doctors is illegal

questions.explanation: The summary cites the official figure: the government admits about 3,000 doctors emigrate yearly — and the mass exodus includes many Master's-degree-seeking graduates and nurses.

questions.question: Why are study visas the preferred route for households 'japa-ing' abroad, according to the tales Bepo hears?

options.text: They cover the holder plus spouse plus children — so whole families relocate, and families sell all their assets to fund them
They are processed in two working days anywhere
They come with free university degrees
They cannot be revoked once stamped

questions.explanation: Study visas allow the holder, spouse and children to travel, so families sell houses, land, cars and household goods; some sold what was not theirs, some fled unpaid loans.

questions.question: A Nigerian who switches from driving to a maintenance job abroad can earn how much per day?

options.text: About $500 a day — roughly ₦800,000 daily
About $50 a day — roughly ₦80,000 daily
About $1,500 a day — roughly ₦2.4 million daily
Minimum wage — about $10 a day

questions.explanation: The summary gives the maintenance-job switch at about $500 a day, ≈ ₦800,000 daily — and notes cabbies outrun toilet-cleaners in pay even in developed economies.

questions.question: Why did Jare weep, despite landing a job in London?

options.text: Caring for an old couple in London docked the dignity of a former banker — he could not bear what it made of him
His visa was refused at the arrival hall
His wife refused to fund his Master's degree
He broke his leg in the freight yard

questions.explanation: Jare left a banking job and wept to discover that caring for an old couple in London — lawful, honest, paying — still docked his dignity. The japa dream does not only deliver pounds; it also delivers what those pounds were bought with.

questions.question: What had Riike, a Nigerian now in the United States, achieved in under three years?

options.text: She bought two houses in Ibadan and has brought two of her sisters over
She finished a nursing degree and was posted to a London hospital
She opened a petrol station outside Lagos
She built a mansion on the island within two years

questions.explanation: Riike's household went fee-free for schooling; in under three years she bought two Ibadan houses, brought two sisters, and was still working to clear visa hurdles for her youngest brother, Wemimo.

questions.question: What emergency-response fact from the tales Bepo hears made the deepest point about the UK health system?

options.text: A three-year-old who had a seizure drew two ambulances plus a car in under five minutes — and had her birthday in hospital with gifts from staff
Ambulances never come to private homes in Britain
The NHS requires a deposit before any emergency call-out
Paramedics waited two days before attending

questions.explanation: Sola's call with Bepo passes on exactly this: a three-year-old who had a seizure drew two ambulances plus a car in under five minutes — birthday in hospital, gifts showered by staff. It lands as the sharpest contrast between the two systems.

questions.question: Where does Mrs Mary Ladele — the woman watching a Nollywood film at 1 p.m. with sleeping children — live?

options.text: GRA, the Government Residential Area in Abuja
Lekki Phase 1, behind Stardom Schools
Adeniyi Jones, Ikeja — Bepo's room in that chapter
Ifo, Ogun State — Fafore's home

questions.explanation: The parallel thread in Chapter 4 places Mary Ladele in GRA, watching Nollywood at 1 p.m. Her husband Dele is a senior civil servant in Abuja. The nightmare with Ayesoro is what follows.

questions.question: Why does Lyi suspect the visas were refused on paternity grounds rather than for any other reason?

options.text: Visa rules require paternity evidence for applicants below 18 — and the DNA test had already shown Favour is not Ibe's daughter
The embassy said so in a letter read on television
His father told him so on the phone
The school administration leaked the DNA result to him

questions.explanation: Lyi is the only member of the family who has quietly connected the dots: DNA showed Favour (15, SS2) is not Ibe's daughter, and below-18 visa rules demand paternity evidence — so the refusal makes sense to him, if not to his father.

questions.question: What did Yoruba braids such as suku, kojusoko and onilegogoro (and the bridal art of irun didi) fetch per head in the UK, according to the bridal-art plan the embassy case reveals?

options.text: $100 per head — about ₦160,000
$10 per head — about ₦16,000
$1,000 per head — about ₦1.6 million
A flat ₦5,000 per head

questions.explanation: Mrs Ignatius had learned tailoring, hairdressing and irun didi, and went in for specific Yoruba braids with the promise of $100 per head in the UK — about ₦160,000 — the arithmetic that pulled them toward the move.

questions.question: How large was the Stardom staff cooperative's purse when the MD caught sight of the parked cars?

options.text: ₦95 million, of which over ₦50 million had been loaned out
₦9.5 million, fully loaned out
₦950 million, mostly as fixed deposits
₦50 million, entirely unloaned

questions.explanation: The accountant, Jeremi Amos, explains the soft soothing position: the cooperative purse held about ₦95 million, over ₦50 million was out as loans, and deductions came straight from source. No one was stealing.

questions.question: Who chairs the family board that met after the parked-cars inspection to restrain the cooperative?

options.text: Chief Mrs Solape Bayo — the MD's mother
Mrs Ibidun Gloss herself
Martins Bayo, the non-executive director
Oye Bayo, the board secretary

questions.explanation: Mrs Solape Bayo convened the family board — Martins (non-exec) and Oye Bayo (last-born, board secretary) — and delivered the verdict: no staff member may borrow more than ₦250,000, every loan needs the MD's sign-off, and the management must be informed of cooperative elections.

questions.question: Why can't Mr Fafore simply rent near Stardom in Lekki?

options.text: Lekki two-bedroom rents pass ₦2 million per annum, far beyond his ₦175,000 salary
Stardom policy forbids staff from living in Lekki
He prefers village life on principle
His house in Ifo is a Stardom-provided residence

questions.explanation: Fafore — 22 years of service, Most Punctual Teacher twice — wakes at 4 a.m., leaves by 4:30 and reaches Stardom by 6, naps at his desk, and still cannot afford a Lekki two-bedroom over ₦2 million per annum. Hence the self-built, unplastered house in Ifo.

questions.question: What do the Gbayi family send Stardom in the run-up to Open Day — and why that gift?

options.text: Packets of beverages — Mrs Nike Gbayi's husband works for a leading beverage company
Bottles of fine wine from an owned vineyard
School bags for the deserving
Fuel vouchers for all drivers

questions.explanation: Open Day gifts cut both ways — parents bring complaints and gifts. The Gbayis, whose principal-job connection is the beverage industry, drop packets of beverages; parents also come loaded with complaints for any teacher who steps on a pupil's toes.

questions.question: Where did the Banky–Tosh feud begin, long before the prefect-squabble speech?

options.text: The JSS 3 Best Dancer hip-hop finale — judges crowned Banky on a 3–2 vote, and Tosh's mother never accepted the result
The PTA treasurer election their mothers contested
The two parties' primaries their fathers contested
A chess final in SS1 decided on a disputed rule

questions.explanation: The houses were political rivals — two leading parties, a PTA treasurer contest their mothers fought — but the sons' powder-keg lit at the JSS 3 Best Dancer hip-hop final: Banky took it 3–2 over Tosh, and Tosh's mother complained bitterly about the judging.

questions.question: What is the 'Point of No Return' visited at the end of the Badagry excursion?

options.text: The jetty on the Badagry beach from which enslaved Africans were shipped across the Atlantic
A memorial park in Lagos for returnee slaves built in 1925
The cliff edge at Gurara Falls the students dare each other to stand on
The First Storey Building Ajayi Crowther used as a mission house

questions.explanation: The Badagry leg closes at the Point of No Return — the jetty that shipped human cargo to the Americas. Standing there is what undoes Bepo and turns his 'japa' arithmetic into 'chains on the economy, not on the wrists.'

questions.question: Who discovered Gurara Falls (Niger State), and when, according to the summary?

options.text: A Gwari hunter named Buba, around 1748 — nearly two centuries before Europeans arrived in 1925
Rev. John S. McGee in 1852, from his Igede-Ekiti mission base (that is Ikogosi)
A daughter of Oduduwa, in 1140 AD (that is Erin-Ijesa / Olumirin)
Its discoverer is unknown and unknowable

questions.explanation: Gurara was discovered by a Gwari hunter named Buba around 1748 — nearly two centuries before Europeans reached it in 1925. Ikogosi (1852, McGee) and Erin-Ijesa (1140 AD) are different waterfalls.

questions.question: By when had Bepo's lapsed passport become an emergency?

options.text: By the first quarter of 2022
In 2020, when the pandemic began
Only after the UK appointment was signed in 2023
At the 2021 WASSCE celebration

questions.explanation: Two years of procrastination plus COVID-19 made renewal impossible; by the first quarter of 2022 he could no longer bear the Lagos crowds — and the Ibadan option opened up.

questions.question: What extra token did Bepo part with at the capture hall when officials offered to expedite his renewal?

options.text: ₦2,000 as a courtesy
₦20,000 for the booklet
$200 in cash
Nothing — he refused on principle

questions.explanation: When officials offered to expedite, Bepo parted with an extra ₦2,000 as courtesy — learning the terrible waiting game up close, distinct from Tai's ₦100,000 + ₦20,000 fees for the 10-year 64-page booklet.

questions.question: What did Tai, the unofficial agent in Ibadan, charge for a 10-year 64-page passport — and what extra for capture?

options.text: ₦100,000 for the booklet, plus a further ₦20,000 to expedite capture
₦10,000 flat, government tariff
₦1,000,000 — a bribe, plain and simple
Nothing — the Ibadan office was free

questions.explanation: Tai, a business-centre operator with a direct line at Agodi-Gate, charges ₦100,000 for the 10-year 64-page booklet plus ₦20,000 to push it to capture within about three weeks — the same service the government promises at a fraction of the cost.

questions.question: What full name does the farewell banner stretched across the main hall reveal for 'Bepo'?

options.text: Adebepo Adewale
Adewale Adebepo
Adepoju Adewale
Oluwole Adebepo

questions.explanation: 'Adebepo Adewale' goes up publicly for the first time: 'To our most committed principal…' — the school learns what its principal is actually called.

questions.question: What happens in the students-versus-staff novelty match at the farewell?

options.text: The referee — later identified as Audu — rejects goals and awards five penalties; the game ends in a goalless stalemate
The staff win 3–1 with a last-minute goal
The match is abandoned after a fight
The students win 2–0 in a heart-stopper

questions.explanation: Wednesday's match vs staff: the referee (Audu) repeatedly disallows goals, awards five penalties, and the game ends stalemate — a fittingly stubborn farewell, goals left standing for the kids.

questions.question: What did the arts team argue — and win with — at the farewell debate on Nigeria's strongest cultural-export?

options.text: That film, music and culture — not science and technology — are Nigeria's strongest international exports
That crude oil remains the only real export
That agriculture is Nigeria's only viable export
That Nigeria has no exports worth debating

questions.explanation: Friday's debate asked which Nigeria gains most from — artistic/cultural output or science/technology. The arts team won, citing film, music and culture as the strongest international exports; Bepo watches his seed pay off.

questions.question: Which 'pillar' qualities did the MD name in Bepo at the farewell — earning him the school's highest disengagement gift?

options.text: Skill, drive, empathy and morals
Speed, courage, wealth and fame
Punctuality, neatness, thrift and silence
Talent, memory, strength and height

questions.explanation: The MD recounts that her father, Chief David Aje, hired Bepo after he never showed for the interview — only a chat — and waited eight days; she praises his pillar qualities of skill, drive, empathy and morals, and calls him a blessing to Stardom.

questions.question: Which song erupts at Stardom on the Monday after Bepo returns?

options.text: The Stardom school anthem — 'We're Stars, we're Stars! We're Stars of Stardom! We're Stars and we have won!'
The National Anthem, second stanza
'Nigeria, we hail thee'
A Yoruba praise chant for the principal

questions.explanation: Monday at Stardom is jarring: the school turns down, until shouts echo — 'I'm back! I'm back! I didn't go!' — and the assembly erupts in tears, dancing and the Stardom anthem, with Bepo in his place.
